geometry_edits.rationale: Strengthen the base connection to the street so the mass reads as one active building rather than two colliding blocks.
Broaden the plinth to improve the public threshold at ground level.
Open the split to create a clearer, more usable courtyard seam.
Increase the void contribution so the subtraction becomes legible in section and elevation.

graph_edits.rationale: Convert the dominant split into a true courtyard logic so the void becomes a legible public figure instead of a thin separation.
Keep a grounded base so the building reads as one street-facing body with an active threshold.
Thicken the street plinth to strengthen the public edge and reduce the floating-box effect.
Open the central seam enough to read as usable public space rather than a construction gap.
Enlarge the puncture slightly so it contributes to a clearer accessible void logic.

rationale: The candidate reads consistently as a compact split block in all four views, so it is not incoherent, but it is too generic and box-like for the neighborhood-living brief. The parcel is respected in orientation and containment, but the dominant gesture does not turn into a legible public threshold at the access edge; the blue frontage is answered only weakly by the central split and small apertures. The void is present yet underscaled and semantically thin, reading more like a gap between two solids than a usable court, terrace, or entry seam. Sectionally, the mass remains flat and low with no real roof/section invention, so it fails to express the required active ground plus calm upper hierarchy. It has good repair integrity because the geometry is clean and the views agree, but the visible form is not yet a plausible neighborhood-living massing solution.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is a tower-like mixed-use prism; candidate is a low split box and does not share the tall sectional logic.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Stepped/tapered massing can work when the upper profile is subordinate to a clear urban base.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference is a slender high-rise; the candidate has no comparable vertical hierarchy or tower semantics.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A single mass can remain legible while a subtle lean or taper modulates the silhouette.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference depends on a very low pavilion/marker relationship, unlike this bifurcated block.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A compact base with a distinct minor vertical element can clarify public edge and program entrance.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate lacks the continuous inhabited section; its split reads as a simple voided box rather than a spatial ribbon.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A continuous sectional gesture with a meaningful courtyard/terrace can support neighborhood living.

warnings: Visible form is coherent across views but remains a generic two-block composition.
Public-edge response is weak relative to the verified frontage/access edge.
Non-stair silhouette is low because the silhouette has no meaningful sectional logic, not because steps are present.
No active ground threshold is clearly established at the frontage.
